Synopsis:
Dolor Soliloquy at Figaro's, the final stage of the Serial Killer Quest just before the Murder Tribunal. Dolor has take Figaro as hostage and will say this speech if he sees the players.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SerialKiller_Dolor_Soliloquy.json: This is the climactic confrontation of the Serial‑Killer quest: Dolor (a zealous cultist of Bhaal) has taken Master Figaro Facemaker hostage and is midway through a ritualized, rapturous speech as the players arrive. Off‑screen Figaro is paralysed and helpless on a workbench; if Devella survived earlier beats she may also be present and paralysed nearby. Dolor is surrounded by a selection of cutting implements and holds oversized tailor’s shears to Figaro’s throat while taunting him as his “crowning achievement.” Players may enter from different doors (one may be missing because they destroyed it), and Dolor will deliver this soliloquy on sight — the scene immediately precedes the Murder Tribunal and can be interrupted by the party.

- LOW_Figaro_SellingThings.json: Dialog with Figaro in order to access the cosmetic elements. Before and After Dolor try to kill him.

- LOW_HighberrysHouse_OnlyRoger.json: Dialogue between the players and Roger Highberry in the Serial Killer situation. This dialog will be used while de Wine Festival and if Cora dies.

context: This is the climactic confrontation of the Serial‑Killer quest just before the Murder Tribunal: Dolor, a zealous cultist of Bhaal, has taken Master Figaro Facemaker — a haberdasher/tailor — hostage and is midway through a ritualized, rapturous speech. Figaro (and, if she survived earlier beats, Devella) are paralysed and helpless on a workbench while Dolor rhapsodizes over a spread of cutting implements and presses oversized tailor’s shears to Figaro’s throat, calling him his “crowning achievement.” The party can enter from different doors (one entrance might already be destroyed by the players), and Dolor will deliver this soliloquy on sight; the scene immediately precedes the Murder Tribunal and can be interrupted by the players. The provided dialogue samples show variations of the same moment depending on which door the players use and whether Devella is present.
